title: Cancel and on_error: continue mean different things in every interactive/file command — and confirm cannot be cancelled at all
existing_state: Pressing Cancel in a script prompt does a different thing depending on which command opened it: readfile's picker aborts the entire run via CommandResult.Exit(ScriptExitStatus.Cancelled) (Services/Scripting/Commands/ReadFileCommand.cs:360-370); input, choose, and multiselect return a plain step Fail bypassing ApplyOnError even though their other failures honor on_error: continue (InputCommand.cs:61-65/82, ChooseCommand.cs:58-62/78, MultiselectCommand.cs:56-60); writefile's save dialog returns Fail, or Suppressed under on_error: continue (WriteFileCommand.cs:42-51). Meanwhile `confirm` offers no cancel path at all: ESC and window-close map to the No button (ConfirmCommand.cs:114 CancelButton = btnNo), so the script always proceeds with the literal string 'false' stored (ConfirmCommand.cs:41-42) — an operator who wants to abort the run at a confirmation gate cannot express that from the dialog. on_error: continue is equally inconsistent: readfile and writefile path/extension validation errors return CommandResult.Ok(message) — plain success, not even flagged as suppressed (ReadFileCommand.cs:62-65, 84-87, 95-98; WriteFileCommand.cs:58-59) — while every other command goes through ApplyOnError → Suppressed; and playsound silently treats an omitted on_error as continue (PlaySoundCommand.cs:127-134), documented only in a code comment. Finally, the unattended-run dialog gate exists only in readfile (AllowFileSelectionDialogs check, ReadFileCommand.cs:237-238); writefile with a relative path pops its modal save dialog unconditionally (WriteFileCommand.cs:175-182), so a scheduled job stalls on an invisible dialog.
recommendation: Define one contract and apply it across the commands: (1) Cancel produces one consistent result — e.g. Fail with a 'cancelled by user' message routed through ApplyOnError, plus an optional per-step on_cancel: fail|exit|continue for scripts that want the readfile abort-the-run behavior, and a <into>_cancelled marker variable so scripts can branch; (2) give confirm an optional allow_cancel: true that adds a Cancel button distinct from No, failing the step under the same contract (register the key in the parser tables, ScriptParser.cs:138); (3) every on_error: continue path returns CommandResult.Suppressed (route through ApplyOnError), never bare Ok, so _last_error and the canvas suppressed-error styling work; (4) gate writefile's save dialog on context.AllowFileSelectionDialogs like readfile; (5) make playsound's continue-by-default explicit in docs/validator.
user_benefit: Script authors can predict what Cancel and on_error: continue actually do instead of learning per-command folklore, operators get a real 'abort here' affordance at confirmation gates, and scheduled jobs stop stalling on invisible save dialogs.

evidence.note: cancel = Exit(Cancelled); continue = bare Ok; only command gated on AllowFileSelectionDialogs
